text:
alex: CI alert — image publish failing on registry when pushing build 2026-03-15. Started after I switched Dockerfile to a 2-stage build. Error is "unexpected EOF" while uploading a layer. Anyone seen this?

ci-bot: build-2026-03-15 · publish job failed · exit code 1
    logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/2026-03-15/12345

alex: paste of tail of registry log:
```
time="2026-03-15T10:12:03Z" level=error msg="http: unexpected EOF" request_id=abc123 layer_dgst=sha256:deadbeef
```

jamie: did you try a rebuild with --no-cache? sometimes cache mismatches cause odd layer uploads to break with EOFs.

alex: yeah did that, same error. tried on my laptop and in CI.

morgan: @alex can you paste the `docker build` command and exact push output? also which registry host (harbor/gcr/ecr)?

alex: command: `docker build -t registry.internal.redwood/release/service:canary -f Dockerfile .` then `docker push registry.internal.redwood/release/service:canary` push output shows many chunks then:
```
... Pushing layer sha256:deadbeef... UPLOAD 99%
error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = unexpected EOF
```

theo: we rotated registry certs two days ago — but that usually gives TLS errors, not EOF. @infra-oncall any recent registry restarts?

infra-oncall: we had a rolling restart of the registry nodes last night around 02:00 UTC for kv upgrade. No errors reported in healthchecks but I can tail the storage logs.

jamie: curious if the multi-stage change bumped the produced layer size or changed chunking. Could be our proxy (nginx) cutting long connections. Try smaller --max-concurrent-uploads or change chunk size?

alex: good idea. Trying `export DOCKER_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=120; export COMPOSE_HTTP_TIMEOUT=120` and rerun.

ci-bot: rebuild queued (no-cache + increased timeouts).

morgan: if it fails again can you run with `docker --debug` and capture the raw HTTP calls? we need to see if the client received FIN or server reset.

alex: rerun failed again. attaching debug snippet:
```
DEBU[0456] Pushing blob: sha256:deadbeef
DEBU[0456] chunked transfer ended unexpectedly: EOF
```

theo: sounds like server side is terminating the upload mid-chunk. @infra-oncall can you grep registry logs for that request_id (abc123)?

infra-oncall: found it — storage backend returned io: read/write on closed pipe around same time as upload. Looks like a transient redis connection hiccup that triggered the registry to abort the upload.

jamie: ah — when storage layer errors we abort multipart upload which results in EOF client-side. Can we restart the storage proxy or bump retries?

infra-oncall: I've restarted the registry pod on canary cluster and bumped storage retry window. CI rebuilds should be unblocked in ~2min.

ci-bot: rebuild succeeded · publish job passed · image pushed: registry.internal.redwood/release/service:canary

alex: confirmed, push succeeded after the restart. Thanks for the fast triage everyone. I'll open a small follow-up PR to add retry logic around uploads and a note in the runbook about the storage-proxy sashimies.

morgan: can you also add a short healthcheck alert for read/write errors from storage backend? we should catch this earlier.

alex: adding to TODOs. :+1:

theo: nice work triaging — short postmortem entry in incidents channel?

alex: will do.
